newsitem.title: INDIA: Speculators prop up select shares at Calcutta.
newsitem.headline: Speculators prop up select shares at Calcutta.

text.p: Select scrips were able to hold onto modest gains on Friday at the Calcutta Stock Exchange (CSE) on short covering by speculators, brokers said.

They said speculators were taking advantage of the recent sharp fall in prices to cover their positions. Brokers said the speculators' gameplan was now to push up prices to higher levels at which they could short sell once again.

"Not much should be read into the modest gains today. The markets looks very bad and I do not see why share prices should move up and maintain," said Suresh Somani of brokers Ratnabali Securities Ltd.

"Speculators are controlling the entire market movement. There are no investors, either domestic or foreign. A major fall is in the offing and speculative sellers are just taking a breather before launching a fresh offensive," Somani added.
With foreign institutional investors (FIIs) off the market, volumes were sharply down and only few select blue-chips were attracting speculative interest, traders said.
